page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.metal-24xl is a compute-optimized bare-metal server instance featuring 96 physical cores powered by AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors running at 2.8 GHz. It provides a non-hyperthreaded 1:1 core-to-vCPU ratio with 96 vCPUs and 192 GB of DDR5 memory, yielding 2 GB of memory per core. The server includes 5,700 GB of NVMe SSD local instance storage and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps. Hardware cryptography is enabled via dedicated AES instruction support.

In synthetic benchmarks, c8gd.metal-24xl demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded compute performance, scoring in the top 10% for multi-core stress-ng tests, Geekbench multi-core scores, software compilation using Clang, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression. Cache and memory subsystem throughput are supported by 36 MB of L3 cache, delivering uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 481.5 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core processing capabilities fall into average ranges, as seen in single-core stress-ng and Geekbench evaluations, indicating that workloads benefit primarily from parallel execution across all 96 cores rather than single-threaded clock speed.

By combining high core density with integrated NVMe SSD local storage, the instance delivers high resource efficiency for sustained, parallelized execution without requiring external storage attachments. Performance metrics show top-tier results in Redis SET operations reaching 199.87 million operations per second, high static web serving throughput, and strong database operation benchmark scores. These characteristics make c8gd.metal-24xl suited for high-concurrency database deployments, large-scale software compilation, in-memory caching layers, and parallel data-processing tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gd.metal-24xl is a bare-metal compute-optimized instance built on 96 physical cores of AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors operating at 2.8 GHz. Equipped with 192 GB of DDR5 memory and 5,700 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, this server delivers a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio and a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps. Benchmark results highlight top-tier performance in multi-core compute workloads, software compilation with Clang, memory read bandwidth, and high-concurrency database operations, including Redis SET throughput exceeding 199 million operations per second. While multi-threaded throughput ranks in the top 10%, single-core performance remains average, emphasizing parallel scaling efficiency over single-thread velocity. The server provides strong resource efficiency for compute-heavy and storage-bound workloads, making it well suited for distributed database clusters, parallel data processing, in-memory caching systems, and continuous integration software builds.
